asset_label: interior building zone (ceiling, wall, floor, shaft or room) seen in a photo, or its humidity and leak sensor series
source_note: EPA mold and moisture guidance: indoor RH below 60 percent, ideally 30-50, and wet materials dried within 24-48 hours so mold usually does not grow (https://www.epa.gov/mold/brief-guide-mold-moisture-and-your-home); Table 1 water-damage responses (https://www.epa.gov/mold/mold-remediation-schools-and-commercial-buildings-guide-chapter-4). The 80 percent 30-day running-mean row is the original ASHRAE 160 criterion (https://doi.org/10.1520/stp159920160106) [PUBLIC, secondary], later replaced by a mold index. Image rows without a URL are the team's own descriptions [team-proposed, validate]. Sensor rows are graded deterministically by cascade.building.water: each carries a 'family' (the indicator it reads), 'min' (inclusive) and 'max' (exclusive). The unified mapping is the team's own [team-proposed, validate].

rows.criterion: No visible staining, tide marks, efflorescence, mold, swelling or active water on the surface in view [team-proposed, validate]. S0 means nothing visible, not a dry assembly.
Water stain or tide mark with no sign of active wetness [team-proposed, validate].
White mineral deposit on masonry or concrete, a sign of repeated water passage [team-proposed, validate].
Wet or stained-and-sagging ceiling tile: EPA Table 1 says discard and replace (EPA_TABLE1).
Wet gypsum wallboard with no obvious swelling and seams intact may be dried in place (EPA_TABLE1).
Wet gypsum wallboard with obvious swelling or seams not intact: remove and replace (EPA_TABLE1).
Visible mold growth; remediate per EPA commercial guide chapter 4 (EPA_TABLE1 URL).
Drips, running or standing water, a spreading wet sheen, or a leak sensor reading wet. Dry within 24-48 hours to prevent mold in most cases (EPA_DRY_WINDOW_H).
Drips, running or standing water, a spreading wet sheen, or a leak sensor reading wet. Dry within 24-48 hours to prevent mold in most cases (EPA_DRY_WINDOW_H).
Indoor RH below 60 percent, ideally 30-50 (EPA_RH_MAX). Needs a working sensor with data in the window.
RH at or above 60 percent for 72 h or more (EPA_RH_MAX; duration RH_SUSTAINED_H [team-proposed, validate]).
30-day running mean RH at or above 80 percent with temperature 5-40 degC (ASHRAE160_RH_30D, original criterion).
Wet for more than 48 h after a leak or storm response (EPA_DRY_WINDOW_H upper bound).
No usable image of the surface, or no sensor data in the window: U, never Dry or RH ok. A zone without a sensor has an unmeasured rain response, not a zero one.
rows.source: project rule (U is never S0) [team-proposed, validate]; RH rows need data in the window per EPA_RH_MAX https://www.epa.gov/mold/brief-guide-mold-moisture-and-your-home

unified_note: Active leak with fire_shock_pathway (water path reaches electrical equipment within WATER_NEAR_PANEL_HOPS) maps to S4 (escalate) [team-proposed, validate].
measurement_note: Sensor families: rh_hourly = latest hourly RH (%RH); rh_sustained_h = hours of the current run at or above EPA_RH_MAX; rh_30d_mean = 30-day running mean RH with the zone temperature in 5-40 degC; wet_duration_h = hours wet after a leak or storm response; leak_sensor = 1 when a leak sensor reads wet.

flags.not_measurable: set when the sensor has no data in the window or the photo cannot show the surface
flags.fire_shock_pathway: set by the problem manager when the water path reaches electrical equipment
